_note: The Gym manifest (WP25a): which grammar points act as selectable form categories, grouped into picker columns. 'point' must match the grammar point title exactly (resolved to ids at request time). 'usage' is the plain-language hover explanation; 'example' is a short illustration. 'nonstandard': forms hidden behind the 'include non-standard words' toggle.

entries.label: Present -ar
entries.usage: Now or regularly, -ar verbs.
entries.example: Eu falo português.

entries.label: Present -er/-ir
entries.usage: Now or regularly, -er and -ir verbs.
entries.example: Como pão e abro a porta.

entries.label: Pretérito perfeito
entries.usage: A finished past action.
entries.example: Ontem falei com ela.

entries.label: Imperfect
entries.usage: The ongoing or habitual past.
entries.example: Quando era criança, falava muito.

entries.label: Future (ir)
entries.usage: What will happen: ir + infinitive.
entries.example: Amanhã vou comer tarde.

entries.label: Conditional
entries.usage: What would happen.
entries.example: Eu gostaria de viajar.

entries.label: Subjunctive
entries.usage: After que — wish, doubt, request.
entries.example: Espero que você fale.

entries.label: Past subjunctive
entries.usage: Hypotheticals: se eu falasse…
entries.example: Se eu falasse, entenderia.

entries.point: Futuro do subjuntivo (quando eu falar, se eu quiser)
entries.label: Future subjunctive
entries.usage: Real future conditions: quando, se, assim que, enquanto.
entries.example: Quando você falar com ela, me avise.

entries.label: Personal infinitive
entries.usage: Infinitive that agrees with its own subject.
entries.example: É melhor partirmos cedo.

entries.label: Imperative
entries.usage: Commands.
entries.example: Fala mais alto!

entries.label: Progressive
entries.usage: Happening right now.
entries.example: Estou comendo agora.

entries.point: Key irregular presents (vou, faço, posso, quero)
entries.label: Irregular presents
entries.usage: The common irregular present forms.
entries.example: Vou ao centro e faço tudo.

entries.label: Irregular preterites
entries.usage: The common irregular preterites.
entries.example: Fui e fiz tudo.

entries.label: Ser (permanent)
entries.usage: For what someone or something simply is — your job, where you are from, what you are like, and what time it is.
entries.example: Eu sou engenheira. — I am an engineer.

entries.label: Estar (temporary)
entries.usage: For how someone feels right now or where something is at the moment — tired, hungry, at home.
entries.example: Eu estou com fome. — I am hungry.

entries.label: Ter (have)
entries.usage: For what you have — and also for your age and for being hungry, thirsty or cold, where English says 'I am'.
entries.example: Eu tenho duas irmãs. — I have two sisters.

entries.label: Negation
entries.usage: To say you don't do something, put não straight in front of the verb — and in Brazil you will hear a second não tacked on the end for emphasis.
entries.example: Eu não como carne. — I don't eat meat.

entries.point: Tem / Há — there is, there are
entries.label: Tem / Há (there is)
entries.usage: For saying that something exists or is around — tem in everyday Brazil, há in writing, and há also means 'ago' with a stretch of time.
entries.example: Tem um banco nesta rua? — Is there a bank on this street?

entries.label: Reflexives
entries.usage: For things you do to yourself or to each other — getting up, being called a name, meeting — with me, se or nos in front of the verb.
entries.example: Eu me levanto às seis da manhã. — I get up at six in the morning.

entries.label: Tenho falado (lately)
entries.usage: For something you have been doing again and again lately — never for one single finished event, which is the trap for English speakers.
entries.example: Ultimamente eu tenho trabalhado demais. — Lately I've been working too much.

entries.label: Reported speech
entries.usage: For passing on what someone said or asked — disse que for a statement, perguntou se for a yes-or-no question, with the verb stepped back into the past.
entries.example: Ele disse que estava cansado. — He said (that) he was tired.

entries.label: Passive
entries.usage: For saying what was done to something when you are not naming who did it — foi construído in careful Portuguese, vende-se on an everyday sign.
entries.example: O museu foi inaugurado em 1950. — The museum was opened in 1950.

entries.point: Ficar — become, stay, be located, keep on
entries.label: Ficar (become/stay)
entries.usage: One verb doing four everyday jobs: where a place is, staying somewhere, turning happy or angry, and keeping on doing something.
entries.example: A farmácia fica ao lado do banco. — The pharmacy is next to the bank.

entries.label: Tenha / tivesse feito
entries.usage: For hoping something already turned out well, and for saying what would have happened if things had gone differently.
entries.example: Espero que você tenha gostado do presente. — I hope you liked the gift.

entries.label: Articles
entries.usage: o/a/os/as and um/uma.
entries.example: o livro, a casa

entries.label: Adjectives
entries.usage: Adjectives match gender and number.
entries.example: um carro vermelho

entries.label: Possessives
entries.usage: meu/minha, seu/sua.
entries.example: meu amigo, minha casa

entries.label: Demonstratives
entries.usage: this / that / that over there.
entries.example: este dia, aquela noite

entries.label: Contractions
entries.usage: preposition + article fused.
entries.example: no bosque, da cidade

entries.label: Subject pronouns
entries.usage: For saying who is doing something — eu for yourself, você for the person you are speaking to, ele or ela for someone else, and in everyday Brazil a gente for 'we'.
entries.example: Eu sou do Brasil. — I am from Brazil.

entries.label: Gender & plurals
entries.usage: Every thing-word in Portuguese is either an o-word or an a-word, and that choice decides the shape of the words around it; add -s for more than one.
entries.example: O livro está na mesa. — The book is on the table.

entries.label: Question words
entries.usage: For asking where, what, when, who, how, why or how much — the asking word goes first, often followed by é que.
entries.example: Onde fica a estação de metrô? — Where is the metro station?

entries.point: Object pronouns (me, te, o, a, nos)
entries.label: Object pronouns
entries.usage: For the person or thing an action happens to — me, te, o, a, nos — and in Brazil they sit in front of the verb, not after it.
entries.example: Ela me viu no shopping ontem. — She saw me at the mall yesterday.

entries.label: Comparatives
entries.usage: For saying one thing is more, less or just as much as another, with a few one-word exceptions like melhor, pior and maior.
entries.example: São Paulo é maior do que Curitiba. — São Paulo is bigger than Curitiba.

entries.label: Relative pronouns
entries.usage: For adding more about a person or thing you have just named — que does nearly all of it, quem after a small word like com, onde for a place.
entries.example: O bolo que você fez estava ótimo. — The cake you made was great.

entries.label: Pronoun placement
entries.usage: In everyday Brazilian the little words me, te and se go in front of the verb, and words like não, que and sempre pull them forward.
entries.example: Ela me ligou ontem à noite. — She called me last night.

entries.label: Connectors
entries.usage: For joining two ideas — however, therefore, besides, since — and note that embora and mesmo que change the shape of the verb that follows.
entries.example: Está chovendo, por isso vamos de carro. — It's raining, so we'll go by car.

entries.label: Crase & regência
entries.usage: For going to a place or to a person when the word after it takes a — vou à praia, à escola, à médica — and for the small word each verb insists on afterwards: assistir a, gostar de, precisar de.
entries.example: Amanhã vou à praia com as crianças. — Tomorrow I'm going to the beach with the kids.

entries.label: Placement in writing (diga-me)
entries.usage: In careful writing the little pronoun goes after the verb (diga-me), and in the future it even slides inside it (dir-te-ei).
entries.example: Diga-me a verdade, por favor. (formal) — Tell me the truth, please. (formal)

entries.point: Focus & clefts (foi ele que…, é que)
entries.label: Emphasis (é que)
entries.usage: For putting the spotlight on one word — é or foi plus que, the same frame that softens a question into onde é que você mora.
entries.example: Foi ele que quebrou o copo, não eu. — It was he who broke the glass, not me.

entries.point: Register: Brazil, Portugal, and the written norm
entries.label: Register (BR/PT)
entries.usage: For choosing how to sound — everyday Brazilian, the Portugal of tu and estar a, or the formal written norm both countries share.
entries.example: A gente se vê no sábado! (spoken BR) — See you Saturday! (lit. the people see each other)
